cause: Both the family Headset and the project Forest retained the first merged node presentation, so an old cached OLS label masked a newer ETS label for the same node hash.
impact: After the RecordingStage envelope fix, the Graph canvas could still display ols (primary) for an ETS result because the project-level union reapplied a first-family-wins rule.
lesson: Immutable node identity and human-facing presentation have different merge rules: preserve the result identity, but project the newest label and summary deterministically.

evidence.ref: The Headset and project Forest presentation tests each failed with legacy presentation, while the refreshed C2 Graph still showed ols (primary) for the shared ETS model node.
